info.title: Awrad API
info.summary: JSON API served by awrad-server-next to the Android, iOS and web clients.
info.description:
Follows `contracts/api/STYLE.md` (ADR-2026-10-16). Rules are enforced by
`contracts/api/spectral.mjs`; run `npm test` in `contracts/`.

Paths are added slice by slice (`docs/rebuild-plan.md`). Shared building
blocks live under `components` and are referenced, never copied.

servers.description: The deployment's API origin. Web clients use their own origin (same site).

tags.name: accounts
tags.description: Registration, email verification, password reset and the signed-in account (slice 2a).

tags.name: device_sessions
tags.description: Mobile sign-in, token refresh and sign-out (ADR-2026-07-12).

tags.name: account_settings
tags.description: Sessions, password, email and deletion for the signed-in account (slice 2b).

post.summary: Create an account and email a verification code
post.description: Verification-first (ADR-2026-07-12): the account can't sign in until its email is verified with `verify_account_email`. Always `202`, also when the email already has an account, so the response doesn't reveal it. A new code cancels any earlier one.

post.summary: Verify an account's email with the emailed code
post.description: Marks the email verified. It doesn't sign in: the client then calls `create_device_session` (mobile) or `create_browser_session` (web) with the password it already has. A wrong, expired or used code, or an unknown email, is `verification_code_invalid`. After 5 wrong tries the code is spent.
Always `202`. Sent only to an account that exists and isn't verified yet; the new code cancels the old one.
Always `202`. Sent only when the email has an account; a new code cancels the old one.

post.summary: Set a new password with the emailed reset code
post.description: Sets the password and **revokes every session of the account**, mobile and browser. The code also proves the inbox, so an unverified email becomes verified. A wrong, expired or used code, or an unknown email, is `reset_code_invalid`; after 5 wrong tries the code is spent. The client then signs in with the new password.

422.description: `reset_code_invalid`, or `validation_failed` with field codes `password_too_short`, `password_too_long` or `password_too_common` on `/new_password`.

example.title: Reset code invalid
example.detail: the code is wrong, expired or already used

get.description: Accepts either credential; each pipeline checks only its own (ADR-2026-10-15).

get.summary: Every place the account is signed in
get.description: Mobile device sessions and browser sessions together, most recently used first, with the caller's own marked `is_current`. Only active sessions are listed. An account rarely has more than a page.

delete.summary: Sign out one device or browser
delete.description: Ends that session; its next request is `401`. Revoking the caller's own session is the same as signing out. Another account's session, one already ended, or an id that isn't a UUID is `404`.

post.summary: Sign out of all other devices and browsers
post.description: Ends every session of the account except the caller's own.

post.summary: Change the password while signed in
post.description: Needs the current password. Signs out every other device and browser and keeps the caller signed in. The account's email gets a notice that the password changed.

Needs the current password. Emails a 6-digit code to the NEW address; nothing changes until `confirm_email_change`. Always `202` for a valid request: if the new address already belongs to another account, that address gets a notice instead of a code, so the response doesn't reveal it. A new request cancels the previous code.

example.title: Request validation failed
example.detail: new_email is the account's current email

post.summary: Confirm the new email with the code sent to it
post.description: Switches the account to the new address and returns the account. The old address gets a notice of the change. Sessions stay signed in. A wrong, expired or used code is `email_change_code_invalid` (5 tries). If the new address was taken by another account in the meantime, `409 email_taken`.

200.description: The account with its new email.

409.description: The new address now belongs to another account.

example.title: Email taken
example.detail: the new email now belongs to another account

example.title: Email change code invalid
example.detail: the code is wrong, expired or already used

post.description: Needs the current password. Immediately and permanently deletes the account and everything the server keeps for it (sessions, settings, synced data), and ends every session; a browser's cookies are cleared. Practice data stored on devices isn't touched: the apps keep working offline. The address gets a confirmation email. There is no undo. A retry after a lost `204` gets `401`, because the account no longer exists: clients treat `401` after a delete request as done.

post.summary: Sign in on a mobile device
post.description: Creates a device session and returns its tokens. Signing in again from the same installation replaces that installation's session. If the password is right but the email isn't verified, the response is `403 email_verification_required` and the server emails a fresh code (rate-limited), so the client can go straight to the code screen.

password.description: Not checked against the password rules here; a wrong one is `invalid_credentials`.

post.summary: Rotate the refresh token and get a new access token
post.description: Each refresh token works once. `Idempotency-Key` is **required** here: a retry with the same key within 60 seconds returns the same new tokens, so a lost response doesn't sign the device out. Reusing a spent token any other way is `refresh_reuse_detected` and revokes the session. Clients run at most one refresh at a time, keep their tokens on network errors, and drop them only on `401`.

401.description: `refresh_token_invalid` (unknown, expired, or its session ended) or `refresh_reuse_detected` (the session is now revoked). Either way the device is signed out.

example.title: Refresh token invalid
example.detail: the refresh token is unknown or its session has ended

post.description: Revokes the session that owns the refresh token. It takes the refresh token rather than the access token, so it works after an app restart when no access token is held. Always `204`, also for an unknown or already revoked token, so clients can retry it until it succeeds.

get.summary: Get the CSRF token for this browser session
get.description: Works for any browser, signed in or not (ADR-2026-10-15). When the browser has no session cookie yet, this call creates the anonymous session and sets its cookie, so a signed-out browser can then call `create_browser_session`. The web app sends the returned token in `X-CSRF-Token` on every state-changing request. Only the session cookie is read here; a bearer token is ignored.

200.description: The session's CSRF token. Sets the session cookie if there wasn't one.

post.description: Sets the Phoenix session cookie (and the remember-me cookie when `remember_me` is true). Needs the session cookie and CSRF token that `get_browser_csrf_token` gives any browser. Signing in renews the session, so the response carries the new CSRF token. An unverified email gets `403 email_verification_required`, and the server emails a fresh code (rate-limited). A repeat with the same `Idempotency-Key` signs in again rather than replaying, because a stored response can't set the cookie (STYLE §10).

remember_me.description: Keep the browser signed in for 14 days (sliding). Defaults to true.

200.description: Signed in. The session cookie is set.

delete.description: Deletes the session and remember-me cookies and the server-side session token.

bearerAuth.description: Mobile clients. Short-lived access token bound to a device session (ADR-2026-07-12).

cookieAuth.name: _awrad_session
cookieAuth.description: Browser clients. Phoenix session cookie: httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax (ADR-2026-10-15). The cookie name is a placeholder until the server scaffold fixes it.

csrfToken.name: X-CSRF-Token
csrfToken.description: Required with cookieAuth on every state-changing request. Fetch it from `get_browser_csrf_token`.

Uuid.description: Lowercase, hyphenated UUID. User-owned entities use client-generated UUIDv4 (STYLE §4).

Instant.description: RFC 3339 instant in UTC with a `Z` suffix. Field names end in `_at`.

LocalDate.description: Calendar day `YYYY-MM-DD`. Field names end in `_date`; practice days use `local_date`.

LocalTime.description: Local time of day, 24-hour `HH:MM`. Field names end in `_time`.

CountDelta.description: A signed whole-number change to a count, for example -3 to undo three taps.

Cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor. Clients must not parse or build it.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details (STYLE §7). Clients switch on `code` only.

title.description: English, for logs. Never shown to users.

code.description: Stable machine code. Clients map it to localized text.

detail.description: English, for logs. Never shown to users.

errors.description: Field validation errors. Empty when the problem isn't about specific fields.

Email.description: An email address, trimmed by the client (contracts/account-model/v1 email_input). Compared case-insensitively. Invalid ones are `validation_failed` with field code `email_invalid`.

Password.description: 12 to 128 Unicode code points after NFC normalisation, no composition rules (contracts/account-model/v1 password_policy). The server also rejects common passwords. Failures are `validation_failed` with field code `password_too_short`, `password_too_long` or `password_too_common`.

EmailCode.description: A 6-digit emailed code, ASCII digits only. Clients normalise what the user typed first (contracts/account-model/v1 email_code_input). Valid for 15 minutes and 5 tries. A malformed code is `validation_failed` with field code `code_invalid`; clients never send one.

Account.description: A signed-in account. Its email is always verified (verification-first).

CurrentPassword.description: The account's current password, re-entered to confirm a sensitive change. A wrong one is `validation_failed` with field code `current_password_incorrect`.

AccountSession.description: One place the account is signed in.

id.description: For a device session, the same `id` as `DeviceSession.id` in its sign-in grant.

name.description: Device model for a device session ("Pixel 9"); a browser and system summary for a browser session ("Firefox on Windows"), or null when it couldn't be told. Clients show a generic label for null.

is_current.description: True for the session making this request.

DeviceInfo.description: Invalid values are `validation_failed` with field codes `installation_id_invalid`, `device_name_invalid` or `platform_invalid` under `/device/...`.

installation_id.description: Random UUIDv4 the app creates once per installation and keeps in secure storage.

name.description: The device model, for example "Pixel 9" or "iPhone 16". Shown in the device list.

idle_expires_at.description: Ends after 30 days without a refresh; each refresh moves it.

absolute_expires_at.description: Ends 180 days after sign-in, whatever happens.

access_token.description: Bearer token, valid for 15 minutes. Keep it in memory only.

refresh_token.description: Single use. Keep it in secure storage (Android Keystore, iOS Keychain).

field.description: JSON Pointer into the request body, for example `/daily_target`.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: UUIDv4. Replays the stored result for 24 hours (STYLE §10). Clients send it on every retryable POST.

AcceptLanguage.name: Accept-Language
AcceptLanguage.description: Language for any email this request sends: `en`, `ar` or `ml` (the first supported one wins; default `en`). Clients send the app's current language.

RequiredIdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
RequiredIdempotencyKey.description: UUIDv4, required on this operation. A retry with the same key gets the same result.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Page size. Each list operation documents its own default and maximum.

RequestId.description: Correlates the request in server logs. Include it in bug reports.

CodeSent.description: Accepted. If the email qualifies, a code is on its way. The response is the same either way, so it doesn't reveal whether the email has an account. Clients offer "send a new code" 60 seconds after this response; a `429` with `Retry-After` overrides that.

DeviceSessionGranted.description: The device session and its tokens.

BadRequest.description: Malformed request, wrong types, or unknown fields.

Unauthorized.description: Not authenticated, credential expired, or the wrong scheme for this pipeline.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated but not allowed, including an unverified email.

NotFound.description: Doesn't exist, or isn't visible to this caller. Doesn't say which.

InvalidCredentials.description: Wrong email or password. Doesn't say which.

CsrfTokenInvalid.description: The CSRF token is missing or doesn't match the session.

VerificationCodeInvalid.description: `verification_code_invalid` (wrong, expired or used code, or unknown email), or `validation_failed` for a malformed email or code.

example.title: Verification code invalid
example.detail: the code is wrong, expired or already used

example.title: Request validation failed
example.detail: password must be at least 12 characters

CurrentPasswordRejected.description: `validation_failed`. Field codes: `current_password_incorrect` on `/current_password`; for a new password, `password_too_short`, `password_too_long` or `password_too_common` on `/new_password`.
